summary: Over-the-sink adjustable 2-tier dish drying rack at a $35.00 target price. No supplier quote is obtainable, so economics were run backwards with cost_ceiling.py: maximum landed cost is $13.65 base (target ROAS 2.5), $5.64 pessimistic (ROAS 1.8) and $20.24 optimistic (ROAS 3.5); requiring $5.00 profit per order leaves $8.93 base and $1.18 pessimistic. The arithmetic matches candidate 002 almost exactly, but the physical product does not: this is the heaviest and bulkiest item in the set, a rigid two-tier steel frame, so shipping and dimensional weight will consume far more of the same ceiling. The serious finding is IP: a design patent titled 'Adjustable over the sink dish drying rack' (D1023495) and a second titled 'Multiple tier over the sink dish rack' (D630813) match this product's description exactly, and neither record could be opened to confirm grant date, assignee or live status because the patent sources are blocked. G2 is therefore unknown, which under the rubric is a HOLD. G3 and G4 pass; G6 is unknown.

facts.claim: A design patent titled 'Adjustable over the sink dish drying rack' exists under number D1023495, and a second design patent titled 'Multiple tier over the sink dish rack', described as a two tier over the sink dish rack, exists under number D630813

assumptions: Every rate inside cost_ceiling.py is an ASSUMPTION for a store with no trading history: discount 15/10/5 percent, refunds 12/6/3 percent, chargebacks 1.5/0.7/0.3 percent, packaging $1.50/$1.00/$0.50 across pessimistic/base/optimistic.
Payment fees assume the Shopify Payments US online card rate of 2.9 percent plus $0.30. The owner has no Shopify plan, so this is unconfirmed.
Target ROAS of 2.5 in the base case is an ASSUMPTION about cold-traffic performance, not a prediction.

The $35.00 price is itself derived from Amazon category price-filter buckets rather than any single observed listing, which discovery already labelled ASSUMPTION; it sits inside the brief's $25 to $60 band.

The model's base refund rate of 6 percent is likely optimistic for this product type given the sink-span fit problem and post-delivery rust complaints, but it has not been raised because no competitor review evidence exists for this run to justify a specific higher number.

data.method: cost_ceiling (reverse economics). No supplier quote obtainable, so contribution margin is not computable; the maximum bearable landed cost is reported instead.
data.price_label: ESTIMATE - derived from Amazon category price-filter buckets, not a single observed listing; inside the brief's $25-$60 band

G2.reason: Screen only, not legal advice. A design patent titled exactly 'Adjustable over the sink dish drying rack' (D1023495) and a second titled 'Multiple tier over the sink dish rack' (D630813) match this product's description word for word. Design patents protect ornamental appearance, so whether a specific sourced rack infringes depends on a visual comparison that could not be made: patents.google.com and image-ppubs.uspto.gov are blocked, so no drawing, grant date, assignee or live status was obtainable. This is the largest IP exposure across the four candidates and must be cleared before any sourcing. Under the rubric, unknown means HOLD.

G3.reason: No CPSC recall found for any non-powered dish drying rack; the only recalls in this search space are dishwashers recalled for electrical fire hazards, a different product class entirely. No health, medical, safety or efficacy claim is needed to sell a drying rack. Residual physical hazards are minor: exposed wire ends and cut edges on cheap stampings, and a chipped coating on carbon steel that rusts.

G4.reason: Not listed in Meta's Restricted Goods and Services, TikTok's prohibited industry entry list, or Shopify's Acceptable Use Policy restricted categories.

G6.reason: The arithmetic is identical to candidate 002 ($13.65 base, $5.64 pessimistic, $8.93 base with $5 profit required), but the physical product is the heaviest and bulkiest in the set. A rigid two-tier steel frame carries a dimensional-weight penalty on tracked US air freight that the same ceiling will absorb far less comfortably than a flat-packing fabric organizer does. Without a landed quote it is not possible to say which side of $13.65 this falls on, and the honest answer is unknown rather than a guess.

operational_risks: Heaviest and bulkiest candidate of the four: a rigid two-tier steel frame carries a dimensional-weight penalty that directly attacks the $13.65 ceiling, and it is also the most expensive of the four to take back on a return
Return freight on a rigid multi-kilogram item will in most cases exceed the entire contribution on the order, so a refund here is worse than a lost sale
Sink-span fit is a genuine sizing problem, not a cosmetic one: the 'adjustable' feature exists precisely because sinks vary, and a rack that does not span the customer's sink is an immediate return
Transit damage is the top fragility risk: bent tiers, sprung welds and scratched chrome on a rigid frame shipped 12 days in a soft carton
Rust and coating chip complaints arrive weeks after delivery, typically after the return window closes but inside the chargeback window, so they land as disputes rather than returns
Assembly steps and missing small parts (drip tray, spout, utensil holder, cutting-board hook) are a support-load multiplier
Two or three finish variants (stainless, black, bronze) plus a possible one-tier and two-tier split pushes SKU count toward the rubric's operational complexity penalty
Not seasonal, which is the one clear operational advantage this candidate has
The 12-day tracked delivery promise is the hardest to keep here of the four, because heavy rigid parcels are the first to be downgraded to slower lanes when freight capacity tightens
